title: Timor-Leste becomes 11th member of ASEAN’s parliamentary assembly
summary: Timor-Leste's admission as AIPA member this year follows its official ASEAN membership in 2025

blocks.text: Parliamentary leaders in Southeast Asia attend the 47th Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly General Assembly on November 18, 2026.
Timor-Leste's admission as AIPA member this year follows its official ASEAN membership in 2025
MANILA, Philippines – Timor-Leste officially became the newest member of the regional parliamentary organization of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Wednesday, November 18.
The young nation was formally admitted to the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA) after the organization considered its status during the general assembly on Wednesday afternoon in Makati.
AIPA is the center of communication among legislative bodies in the ASEAN, and seeks to promote cooperation and understanding among the member-parliaments.
Timor-Leste’s admission followed its inclusion as member-state of ASEAN in 2025, around 13 years after it gained observer status in the ASEAN.

Resolutions passed by the AIPA are non-binding, but the gathering is a hub for insights and best practices that participating lawmakers can bring back to their home countries to inform their lawmaking.
Ahead of its admission to the AIPA, House Speaker Bojie Dy, who serves as AIPA president, offered Timor Leste a taste of Filipino hospitality in his speech.
“In Filipino homes, when another guest arrives at mealtime, the plates do not get smaller. We simply put more rice in the pot. That is how we welcome Timor-Leste,” Dy said.
“To our friends from Timor-Leste: You have a place at this table, and there is more than enough rice for you,” he added.
European Parliament in ASEAN delegation chair Wouter Beke also congratulated Timor Leste national parliament president Maria Fernanda Lay on the “historic accession” of Timor-Leste to the AIPA.
“A proud milestone for our parliamentary diplomacy,” it said on X. – Rappler.com
